reviewer_blockers: 21.1-R1: the build.yaml changelog's F7 clause overclaims. It states that ArrTags 'restores the original poster (or removes the ArrTags image when no baseline was retained) when a saved configuration narrows an owned item's badge selection to empty'. The shipped behavior on that exact trigger does not remove anything when no baseline was retained: `ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.ReadRetainedSource` returns `ArtworkSourceReadResult.Absent` for a session whose `SourcePresence` is `Absent`, so `GenerateCoreAsync` returns `NoSource` before the render and never reaches the ADR-024 empty-selection restore branch. The removal leg of `ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync` is reachable only from the removal/lifecycle-drain trigger and from the recovery-gate resume, which is precisely the qualification `docs/architecture/09-persisted-artwork-rendering.md:276-282` records and that task 20.3 added after the task 20.1 test-quality finding TQR-20.1-04. `build.yaml` reintroduces the uncorrected phrasing into user-facing release metadata (the catalog description and, per `scripts/publish-release.sh`, the GitHub release notes). One-clause wording fix required; no code change.

I re-ran the validation rather than trusting the worker's numbers: `./build.sh build` -> 0 warnings / 0 errors; `./build.sh package` -> `artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip`, 7 entries, 619,561 bytes, packaged `build.yaml` byte-identical to the source (`cmp` clean) and carrying `version: "1.2.0.0"` / `targetAbi: "12.0.0.0"` / `framework: "net10.0"`, and the packaged `ArrTags.dll` reports `1.2.0.0`; `./build.sh test` -> Failed 0, Passed 1927, Skipped 66, Total 1993, matching the worker exactly; the focused packaging/state-location filter -> 11 passed, 0 failed. Six of the eight shipped v1.2 items in the new metadata (G6/G8 units and restart-required surfacing, G7 Extra Large and dropdown order, G9/F8 bounded log subject and render classification, F3 read-only administrator diagnostics, F4 successive-run cursor coverage correctly scoped to scheduled and post-scan triggers, F6 stale-basis re-enqueue) are each supported by the accepted ADR and its implementation note with no overclaim and with the project's own qualifiers ('best-effort', 'a mixed setting states that some paths apply immediately') preserved. The F7 clause is the exception: it attributes the absent-baseline removal to the config-narrowing trigger, which the shipped code path cannot reach, so the metadata asserts a user-visible outcome the plugin does not produce. That is a single open MEDIUM finding tied directly to the task's second acceptance criterion, and it is correctable by rewording one clause. Everything else in the task, including the state/report persistence and the scope discipline, is sound.

findings.summary: The build.yaml changelog claims ArrTags removes the ArrTags image when no baseline was retained on the config-narrowing trigger, but the shipped coordinator path returns NoSource before reaching the restore branch, so no removal occurs there.
findings.detail: build.yaml:41-43 reads: 'restores the original poster (or removes the ArrTags image when no baseline was retained) when a saved configuration narrows an owned item's badge selection to empty'. The parenthetical attaches the removal leg to the configuration-narrowing trigger. In the shipped code that trigger cannot produce the removal: (1) `ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.ReadRetainedSource` (src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.cs:346) returns `RetainedSourceResolution.Failed(ArtworkSourceReadResult.Absent(surface))` whenever an owned session records `SourcePresence == ArtworkImagePresence.Absent`; (2) `ReadSourceAsync` therefore returns that Absent result and `GenerateCoreAsync` (line 216-219) returns `ArtworkGenerationResult.NoSource` before calling the renderer, so the `RenderPassThroughReason.NoDisplayableValue` branch that drives `RestoreEmptySelectionAsync` (line 240-249) is never entered; (3) the absent-baseline removal inside `ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync` (src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:615, 643) is therefore driven only by `ArtworkLifecycleCoordinator.RestoreAsync` (the item-removal / uninstall-drain trigger) and by the recovery-gate resume, not by an empty selection. This is not a new interpretation: the project's own canonical architecture document states it verbatim ('The absent-baseline leg is not reachable through the coordinator's normal generation path: ReadRetainedSource reports the absent retained baseline (Absent), so the coordinator returns NoSource before rendering and never creates that restoration', docs/architecture/09-persisted-artwork-rendering.md:276-282), the task 20.1 test-quality review raised the identical defect as TQR-20.1-04 against that document's wording, task 20.3 corrected it to the publisher-attributed form, and docs/limitations/archive.md:382-387 records the same verification bound. `build.yaml` now carries the pre-correction phrasing into the plugin-catalog description and, per scripts/publish-release.sh, into the GitHub release notes, so an operator reading it would expect the ArrTags image to be removed after narrowing a selection on an item whose baseline was not retained, and would instead observe the badge preserved. Impact is confined to release metadata accuracy (no runtime behavior, no data-integrity or security effect), but it is exactly what acceptance criterion 2 exists to prevent, and the fix is a one-clause reword.

findings.recommended_action: Reword the build.yaml changelog clause so the removal is not attributed to the configuration-narrowing trigger. Simplest correct form: '...and restores the original poster when a saved configuration narrows an owned item's badge selection to empty'. If the removal leg is worth keeping in the catalog text, attribute it to the trigger that reaches it, e.g. '...restores the original poster on narrowing, and the removal and uninstall drains remove the ArrTags image when no baseline was retained'. Then re-run `dotnet run scripts/render-docs-state.cs -- --check` is unnecessary (build.yaml is not a generated surface) but `./build.sh package` must be re-run so the packaged build.yaml matches, and the packaged byte size will change.

findings.summary: The changelog's 'off-step values rejected' is a simplification of accepted limitation V12-G6-1 (a legacy off-step whole-unit value is re-quantized on the next save, not rejected).
findings.detail: build.yaml:29-30 says v1.2 'shows byte-denominated limits in binary units (MB, or KB for the webhook payload) with the exact byte count persisted and off-step values rejected'. For values the operator enters, this is exactly right: `byteLimitToBytes` in src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html:397-414 returns null when `bytes % definition.stepBytes !== 0`, so an entered off-step value is rejected for every field. The simplification concerns only a persisted legacy off-step value: for the whole-KiB and whole-MiB fields the display rounds to a whole unit and the next save writes the nearest whole unit rather than rejecting, which is registered as accepted limitation V12-G6-1 (docs/limitations/accepted.md:704-733) and is disclosed in the shipped documentation. A catalog changelog is not the place for that caveat, and the acceptance criterion is about describing the shipped v1.2 behavior rather than restating every accepted limitation, so this is recorded rather than required.
